To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DLS can be used to resolve protein monomers from aggregates at a mass ratio of the two species in the range from 1 to 1700, depending on the average size of the particles and the scattering characteristics.
DLS can resolve mixtures of proteins and particles at mass ratios between 1 and 1700, depending on particle size and instrument settings.
the resolving power of DLS depends on the size of the particles, the mass ratio of monomer and particles, and the total protein concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantitative analysis of protein samples using DLS.
the resolving power of DLS for binary mixtures and its application to the characterization of proteins.
a quantitative analysis of the resolving power of DLS for protein and polysterene nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the resolution of a protein monomer in the presence of protein particles is not only dependent on the size of the particles but also on the total concentration, the size ratio and mass ratio of the particles.
DLS can be used as a quantitative technique for protein samples, but only under the given conditions.
DLS is capable to distinguish between protein monomer and particles with a size of 50 ± 20 nm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a DLS setup can resolve two protein species if one species is at least 10-fold more abundant by mass than the other and if the hydrodynamic diameters of the species are at least 10–15 nm different.
DLS is not a technique to determine the association state of proteins, but rather a tool for the assessment of particle size distributions and the detection of particle formation.
the resolution of DLS is sufficient to detect monomers in the presence of protein particles, but not to detect protein particles in the presence of monomers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a DLS experiment with a standard setup can provide quantitative information on the size of protein particles in a mixture with monomeric protein, if the monomer is not too abundant.
DLS is not able to distinguish between protein particles with different sizes, if the mass fraction of monomer in a mixture is too high.
DLS is capable of resolving mixtures of monomeric and oligomeric protein species.
